AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Asatryan thanked staff for putting together a wonderful Glendale Tech
  Week. She had the opportunity to attend some of the events and was impressed by their
  turnout and caliber. Asatryan also attended the Glendale Historical Society's Gala at the
  Sanford House together with other council members. Also, she attended as a guest
  speaker, the Northwest Homeowner's Association event together with Mr. Golanian. She
  was pleasantly surprised to see the Planning Director, the City Attorney and Assistant City
  Manager who made themselves available to the residents. One of the issues that came up
  during the meeting was an issue that she had been thinking about for some time which is
  the need for a dog park in the northwest area of Glendale. Asatryan indicated that while
  there are a number of potential projects, City Council is waiting for a report back for a dog
  park in potential locations such as Lot 11, Palmer Park and other sites in South Glendale.
  However, these locations do not serve the northwest neighborhood of Glendale.
  Councilmembers Asatryan and Brotman visited Brand Park and noted that the southwest
  corner of the park might be a potential site for the dog park. Asatryan asked staff for a quick
  memo and a report on converting the SW part of the park, south of the Doctor’s house, to a
  dog park. City Manager Golanian asked for clarification on whether to bring the item back as
  a report or be included in the RFP for the other dog parks. Councilmember Asatryan noted
  that both a quick memo and report would work and it would be good to have it done soon
  10 25 22
  CC

  2
 with just fencing and as part of the RFP for long term design. Brotman seconded.

Councilmember Devine congratulated staff for a successful Glendale Tech Week. She
announced that it is Breast Cancer Awareness Month. She, together with the Mayor
attended an award ceremony that Assemblymember Friedman held at Laura’s Corset
Shoppe located along Brand Blvd. This shop has existed for 100 years. The shop provides
service to patients and survivors of breast cancer. Devine attended the Burbank State of the
City Luncheon and had learned about the City of Burbank Police Department’s drivers’
education program. She indicated that once our city has a new police chief, City Manager
Roubik Golanian and staff will meet with Burbank PD and City Manager to see how the
drivers’ education program works and how it could be implemented in Glendale. Devine
indicated that GUSD Superintendent Dr. Ekchian and one of the GUSD Board Members are
excited about the possibility of collaborating with the city to bring back a drivers’ education
program in the future. Mayor Kassakhian seconded.

Councilmember Brotman re-nominated Sevana Zadorian for the Arts and Culture
Commission.

Councilmember Najarian stated he was a speaker for the Valley Industry & Commerce
Association Panel on the Future of Transportation and met with one of the principals of
BYD, the bus company that will hopefully give the city an electric bus to test out. He spoke
about the recent climate news and indicated that the almost 10-years of efforts by the state
to reduce automobile and power plant emissions was wiped out in one summer as a result
of fires in California. He asked staff to reassess the sustainability plan and bring this issue to
the Sustainability Commission. He suggested that the city put more emphasis on wildfire
suppression and asked staff for a report on how the city can address this issue. Asatryan
seconded.

Mayor Kassakhian attended the Harvest Festival event in Pacific Park, One Glendale Flag
Football Championship Game, the tour of Rockhaven Sanitarium with the Friends of
Rockhaven, and Glendale Tech Week events. He announced that the movie “Gate to
Heaven,” about Artsakh, is being shown at the AMC theatre at the Americana. Kassakhian
attended the renaming of the Wilson Middle School gym after former principal Mr. Richard
Lucas. He announced that Dia De Los Muertos event is coming up at the Glendale Central
Library on November 5th and invited the public to attend. Kassakhian stated that Governor
Newsom appointed former Los Angeles Mayor Antonio Villaraigosa as the infrastructure
advisor to lead the group of local leaders to find out how to take advantage of the funds that
the federal government is allocating for infrastructure programs. Kassakhian asked staff to
see if there is an opportunity for staff to work with neighboring cities on projects of common
interests and to have a discussion on prioritizing infrastructure requests to be submitted to
Mr. Villaraigosa’s office. Asatryan seconded. Kassakhian commented on the emails council
received regarding street vendors and asked staff to provide a report on imposing certain
regulations. Asatryan seconded.

Director of Community Development Bradley Calvert provided a brief update on the city’s
housing element plan which will be agenized for the Housing Authority meeting in the
upcoming weeks.

Mayor Kassakhian asked staff to have the first “Council in your Neighborhood” meeting to
be held at the Rancho area to discuss the preservation of the character of the community
due to the projects being developed around that area. City Manager Roubik Golanian stated
